citations.claim: body 1 position becomes non-finite (NaN) at violating step
body 1 was finite just before violation

counterfactual.change: disabled controller (enabled true->false); controller-driven impulse stacking with existing bodies leads to division producing NaN - without controller no NaN

explanation: At step 2047 bodies 2 and 3 come into contact (gap 0.036) while controller drives body 1 to waypoint. Shortly after, simultaneous collision resolution involving controller forces produces non-finite position/velocity for body 1 (NaN). Prior step 2046 all values finite. Disabling controller removes NaN, confirming controller interaction triggers degenerate impulse/normalization.
vision_note: Tiles 2044-2046 show several blue/orange bodies clustered at the top wall with the large red violating body present in the center-top. At step 2047 the red body vanishes completely leaving only the three blue bodies displaced, the green waypoint becomes visible, and the following tile is blank/black. [disagreement: Picture agrees that a body position becomes non-finite and disappears at the first violating step 2047 after close contact visible in 2044-2046, but it disagrees on identity: the image labels the vanishing violating body as red and distinct from the persisting orange/controller-driven blue bodies, while the explanation claims the controller-driven body 1 itself becomes NaN.]
